routing_reasons: C3 and C4 are supported, and C1 is supported with a record entry other than the visit note; every applicable criterion cites the policy and every cited id exists in the case.

C1_red_flag.explanation: Structured Observations document motor weakness that is both clinically significant and progressive: left ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension were 4/5 on 2026-07-30 and fell to 2/5 by 2026-08-07, with new steppage gait and sensory loss on the later exam. This is an independent structured finding (not note-only) matching the LCD's 'clinically significant or progressive neurologic deficit' and 'clinically significant motor weakness' red flags, and is consistent with the note's assessment of foot drop.
C1_red_flag.policy_quote: Clinically significant or progressive neurologic deficit in the lower extremity

C2_conservative_4wk.explanation: Symptom onset is recorded as 2026-07-27 (Condition/case04-cond-01) and the conservative therapy, naproxen, began 2026-07-30 (MedicationRequest/case04-med-01); the request date is 2026-08-07, only 11 days from onset and 8 days of naproxen use. Both durations fall well short of the four-week threshold the LCD requires for a non-red-flag conservative trial, so this criterion is not met on this record.
C2_conservative_4wk.policy_quote: has not responded to a reasonable trial of conservative management lasting at least four weeks

C3_informs_management.explanation: The structured reasonCode of the 2026-08-07 encounter records an 'urgent spine surgery referral' and the visit note's plan documents urgent referral to spine surgery to evaluate for decompression, indicating a surgical intervention is actively under consideration whose planning depends on the MRI findings.
C3_informs_management.policy_quote: Medicare expects that the information gained from the test will be used for medical decision-making

C4_no_duplicate_imaging.explanation: The record contains no CT scan, prior lumbar MRI, or other imaging study of the spine; there is nothing documenting a duplicative study, so the requested MRI is not shown to duplicate prior imaging.
C4_no_duplicate_imaging.policy_quote: A lumbar MRI that is a duplication of other imaging studies (such as a spinal CT scan) may be unreasonable or unnecessary.

case_summary: This is a request for a lumbar MRI without contrast for a 71-year-old man with acute, 11-day left-sided radiculopathy and progressively worsening left foot weakness, documented by structured exam findings showing strength decline from 4/5 to 2/5. C1 is supported by this objective, progressive motor deficit; C2 is not supported because both symptom duration and conservative therapy (naproxen) are under four weeks; C3 is supported by a structured and narrative record of urgent surgical referral for decompression evaluation; C4 is supported because no other spinal imaging appears in the record. No contradictions were identified and no single missing document is needed to resolve any criterion.
